paper_id: Yang et al. - 2007 - Sea Depth Measurement with Restricted Floating Sensors
title: Sea Depth Measurement with Restricted Floating Sensors
motivation: Harbor siltation monitoring costs $18M/year; existing methods are labor-intensive and require expensive sonar equipment
problem_framing: Define RFS (restricted floating sensors) network; localize floating area (disk center+radius) instead of instantaneous positions
key_insight: Sensors float within known geometric constraints; statistical sampling reveals anchor position and radius, enabling depth calculation
method_signature: FALA: seed MED + non-seed regression analysis on distance samples to estimate floating area parameters
evaluation_criteria: Relative errors: anchor position Ec/r, radius Er/r, sea depth Eh/h
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: RSSI ranging has 150% error; floating model assumption (uniform random) violated near seashore; error propagates with network size
evidence_for_taste: smallest one should be considered the maximum likelihood estimation
RA outperforms GR when sample capacity is larger than 20
directly using those localization approaches does not capture the special movement behaviors
A large sample capacity usually implies a long period of sampling
thinking_moves: Define new sensor mobility class between static and mobile
Recast localization as floating area estimation
Apply computational geometry (MED) to sampled positions
Model uncertainty via uniform distribution, derive statistical estimator
Prefer regression over extreme-value geometric method for robustness
